place_fields.micro_region: Ballari Fort area, Devi Nagar, Ballari
place_fields.vibe: historic fort entrance and access point
place_fields.summary: Gateway 1 to Ballari Fort is an identified gateway/access point associated with Ballari Fort in the Devi Nagar fort area. The Ballari district administration describes the fort complex as having entrance gates and the surrounding fort as a historic site on Ballari Gudda.
place_fields.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon is preferable for exploring the fort area because the official tourism guidance notes that the rocky terrain can be strenuous in midday heat.

planning_attributes.description: A named gateway associated with the Ballari Fort complex in Devi Nagar, Ballari.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach the Ballari Fort area in Devi Nagar, Ballari; the fort is served by road and Ballari railway station is the nearby rail connection described by Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The wider fort complex has steep rocky terrain; suitable footwear, water and sun protection are recommended by Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.notes: The supplied coordinates are preserved exactly. Sources identify the gateway as a nearby/associated point for Ballari Fort but do not provide separate historical details for this specific gateway.

place_fields.vibe: historic hilltop fortress with rocky paths and panoramic views
place_fields.summary: Ballari Fort is a historic fortress on Ballari Gudda. The Ballari district administration describes Upper and Lower Fort sections, while Karnataka Tourism describes the complex as a hilltop defensive site with steep rocky paths, fortifications, cisterns and panoramic views.
place_fields.best_time: Early mornings or late afternoons are recommended to avoid the midday heat while walking the rocky fort terrain.

planning_attributes.description: A historic fort complex on Ballari Gudda, divided into Upper and Lower Fort sections. The Upper Fort contains a citadel, temple, barracks and water-storage wells; the Lower Fort has fortified walls, bastions, pits and entrance gates.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Approximately 1,976 feet above sea level according to Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The Upper Fort is attributed to the Vijayanagara period and Hanumappa Nayaka. Hyder Ali took possession in 1769 and later modified the fort with the help of a French engineer. The Ballari district administration records the local tradition concerning the engineer's grave near the East Gate.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Ballari railway station provides rail access, and the fort is reachable by road from Ballari and surrounding cities. Karnataka Tourism lists Bengaluru, Hyderabad and neighbouring towns among road connections to Ballari.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The terrain is steep and rocky. Karnataka Tourism recommends suitable footwear, sufficient water and sun protection, and advises visitors to avoid touching historic sculptures or walls.
planning_attributes.notes: The supplied coordinates are preserved exactly. Current government tourism sources describe the site as Ballari Fort/Bellary Fort.

place_fields.vibe: active Hindu temple in the historic Ballari Fort area
place_fields.summary: Shri Kote Malleshwara Swamy Temple is a Hindu temple in Narayanappa Compound in the Fort area of Ballari. Karnataka's HRCE directory lists the temple as Sri Kote Malleshwara Swamy temple, Ballary, Ballari District.

planning_attributes.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva in the Fort area of Ballari. Public listings place it on Kote Malleshwara Temple Road in Narayanappa Compound, and the Karnataka HRCE directory lists it as Sri Kote Malleshwara Swamy temple, Ballary.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The temple is located in Narayanappa Compound, Fort, Ballari, Karnataka 583104. The supplied location is preserved exactly.
planning_attributes.notes: The official Karnataka HRCE listing confirms the temple entry but does not provide historical details in its current About Temple section.
